numerical.title: SN2 electronic-structure comparison across C, N, O, and F centers
numerical.model: Cl⁻ + A–Cl, with A–Cl = CH₃Cl, NH₂Cl, OHCl, or FCl; gas phase.
numerical.relation: Related benchmark. This card uses HO⁻ + CH₃Br, so none of these numbers describes its substrate.
numerical.method: ZORA-OLYP/TZ2P; activation-strain analysis at the symmetric transition state for C, N, O and at the transition complex for F. The vacant σ*(A–Cl) energies refer to the isolated substrates under the authors’ orbital convention. Fragments: singlet Cl⁻ (charge −1) and neutral singlet A–Cl; total charge −1, singlet. Strain is relative to the isolated equilibrium fragments; no solvent model.
numerical.interpretation: The acceptor σ* orbital is lower in this series while the fragment interaction becomes more stabilizing. These are a specified orbital energy and an interaction-energy decomposition, not a transferable scalar “coupling degree.”
numerical.limits: Orbital energies depend on the method and orbital convention; the interaction term depends on the chosen fragments and geometry. The F entry is a transition complex rather than the same kind of stationary point as the first three. Values transcribed from Tables 3 and 4; no value for HO⁻ + CH₃Br is implied.
numerical.verification: Numerical transcription checked against primary-source tables/text, 2026-10-13; calculations not reproduced.

insights.method: CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ energies on MP2/6-311++G(d,p) geometries; activation-strain and molecular-orbital analyses. This specifies the energy/geometry protocol; the full orbital/activation-strain analysis settings have not been independently verified in this audit.
insights.finding: For this microsolvated ethyl chloride network, backside SN2 is preferred to anti-E2, and adding water increases the preference. E2 requires greater characteristic substrate distortion; solvation attenuates the fragment interaction.
insights.limits: The teaching card is HO⁻ + CH₃Br, so the computed preference and energies do not transfer.
insights.verification: Model, reported conclusion and energy/geometry method checked in indexed primary-source text; full analysis settings remain incomplete.

insights.model: Isopropyl chloride hydrolysis with explicit water clusters and continuum solvent
insights.method: M06-2X/aug-cc-pVDZ geometry and frequency calculations; explicit and hybrid explicit–implicit solvation.
insights.finding: Across the tested solvation protocols, the computed substitution remains a solvent-assisted, loose SN2-like pathway; the transition structures have substantial SN1-like carbocation character by bond-order analysis.
insights.limits: The card is a generic R₃C–X/anionic-nucleophile two-event core. The paper instead models secondary isopropyl chloride reacting with water; it does not validate the card’s discrete carbocation pathway.
insights.location: Abstract and More O’Ferrall–Jencks bond-order analysis
insights.verification: Model, reported conclusion and energy/geometry method checked in indexed primary-source text; full analysis settings remain incomplete.

insights.method: CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ//MP2/6-311++G(d,p); activation-strain and MO analysis. This specifies the energy/geometry protocol; the full orbital/activation-strain analysis settings have not been independently verified in this audit.
insights.finding: The computed anti-E2 pathway has more characteristic distortion than backside SN2 for this model. Microsolvation weakens nucleophile–substrate interaction and changes the relative pathway preference.
insights.limits: This is a model comparison, not a calculated result for the base and leaving group in this E2 teaching card.
insights.verification: Model, reported conclusion and energy/geometry method checked in indexed primary-source text; full analysis settings remain incomplete.

insights.method: Relaxed distance/angle scans: M06-2X/6-311+G(d,p), Gaussian 16. Single-point ASM/EDA: ZORA-M06-2X/TZ2P, ADF, all-electron, VERYGOOD integration. Gas-phase CN⁻ (charge −1, singlet) + neutral singlet acetone; total charge −1, singlet.
insights.finding: The model’s preferred C(CN)–C(carbonyl)–O angle is about 111°. At smaller angles Pauli repulsion limits approach; at larger angles acetone deformation costs rise. The balance, rather than overlap alone, sets the trajectory.
insights.limits: This card uses a different carbonyl/nucleophile combination. The reported angle is model specific.
insights.verification: Quoted numerical claims and method checked in primary-source tables/text on 2026-10-13.

numerical.title: Orbital interaction and electron donation in a Diels–Alder model
numerical.model: 1,3-Butadiene + acrolein (neutral O) versus 1,3-butadiene + acrolein radical cation (O•⁺).
numerical.relation: Related dienophile. The teaching reaction on this card uses ethene, and the radical-cation pathway is a distinct open-shell mechanism.
numerical.method: ZORA-(U)BP86/TZ2P; fragments are butadiene and acrolein/acrolein radical cation. EDA evaluated at matched transition-state-like geometries with forming C(diene)···Cβ(dienophile) = 2.203 Å. Gas-phase model, no solvent term. Neutral pair: charge 0, singlet; radical-cation pair: charge +1, doublet (unrestricted). Butadiene remains a neutral singlet fragment.
numerical.interpretation: At the matched geometry, ionization changes the EDA orbital term by −27.5 kcal/mol and reduces Pauli repulsion by 18.8 kcal/mol. In the open-shell case, the butadiene π-HOMO and acrolein-cation SOMO have reported overlap S = 0.05 and about 0.7 electron donated into the SOMO under this analysis. The neutral path is concerted asynchronous; the radical-cation path becomes stepwise.
numerical.limits: ΔEorbital is the total EDA orbital-interaction term, S is a dimensionless overlap, and 0.7 electron is a method-specific charge-transfer analysis. None is a diabatic electronic-coupling matrix element H_DA or an intrinsic SORG score. The radical-cation pathway is not assigned the neutral card’s 1333 code.
numerical.verification: Numerical transcription checked against primary-source tables/text, 2026-10-13; calculations not reproduced.

insights.model: Thermal allyl vinyl ether rearrangement to allylacetaldehyde
insights.method: Theoretical reaction-path bonding evolution tracked with the electron localization function (ELF). Full electronic method and basis not verified in this audit; no numerical results are transcribed.
insights.finding: The C3–O bond-breaking and C1–C5 bond-forming electron-density changes do not occur simultaneously. A concerted pathway therefore need not be synchronous at the level of bonding evolution.
insights.limits: The paper studies the same parent rearrangement, but the ELF topology depends on the electronic-structure setup and does not supply a universal timing scale.
insights.verification: Primary abstract checked; full electronic-structure method and basis not verified.

insights.model: Benzene + nitronium in sulfuric acid or water
insights.method: RISM-SCF-cSED: solute electronic structure and liquid solvation determined self-consistently. Full electronic method and basis not verified in this audit; no numerical results are transcribed.
insights.finding: The sulfuric-acid solvation structure changes substantially during C–N bond formation and affects the free-energy surface. Valence-electronic analysis distinguishes important resonance contributions to the Wheland intermediate in gas and solution.
insights.limits: The result concerns the specified solvent models and method; it does not endorse a single charge or resonance weight for every mixed-acid composition.
insights.location: Abstract; solvation free-energy and valence-electronic analyses
insights.verification: Primary abstract checked; full electronic-structure method and basis not verified.
